name: toast
title: Toast
summary: A brief message that appears in a corner and leaves by itself.
description: A brief message that arrives in a corner and leaves by itself: "Link copied", "Deploying…", "Deploy failed" with Retry. <Toast /> is the region (mount it once, near the root of the app); toast({ title, … }) raises one from anywhere. Each toast is a raised card (the selection toolbar's floating surface: surface, shadow.overlay) with the tone's icon (the alert's, in the status-pill tones), a title, a description, an optional action Button and a close Button. Hovering or focusing the region pauses every timer. Behaviour, timing, stacking and announcements come from the Zag toast machine through Ark UI.

anatomy.description: The region (Ark's toaster group): role=region, aria-live=polite, labelled "Notifications" with its hotkey; fixed in its corner, 16px from the edges (and above the safe-area insets), min(356px, 100vw − 32px) wide. Toasts stack in it 8px apart, newest nearest the edge.

One toast: role=status, aria-atomic; data-state=open|closed, data-type. Absolutely placed by the engine through --y, --scale, --opacity and --z-index; a card: radius.card, padding 12px, gap 10px, surface, shadow.overlay. Focusable (tabIndex 0): Escape dismisses it. Carries kbd-instant.
The alert's tone icon (16px, bold, the tone's colour) on the title's first line; a Spinner (sm) while loading. None when neutral. aria-hidden.
Takes the free space: title and description, wrapping (never cut).
A Button (outline, sm) after the text, marked data-toast="action". Calls its handler, then dismisses the toast.
A Button (ghost, xs, square, rounded, muted, X) with a Tooltip, aria-label "Dismiss notification"; marked data-toast="close". On a coarse pointer its hit area reaches 40px.

placement.description: The corner (or edge centre) the toasts arrive in. start and end follow the writing direction.

max.description: Toasts shown at once; the rest wait in a queue.

duration.description: Default time on screen, in ms (each toast may set its own). Paused while the region is hovered or focused, or the page is hidden.

overlap.description: false: every toast shows in full, stacked. true: older toasts tuck behind the newest one and fan out while the region is hovered or focused.

items.title: string
items.loading: boolean? (a Spinner, and it stays until updated or dismissed)
items.action: { label: string, value?: string, onClick?: () => void }? (one Button: onClick runs when it is pressed, an Undo; the action event also reports it, with value or the label)

toasts.description: Toasts raised when the region mounts (the same options toast() takes). Later ones come from toast().

events.action: (value: string, id: string) an action Button was pressed (its own action.onClick runs as well)
events.dismiss: (id: string) a toast left: timed out, closed, Escape, or toast.dismiss()

keyboard: Alt+T moves focus to the region (the engine's hotkey); Tab then walks the toasts and their Buttons
Escape on a focused toast dismisses it
Enter / Space on the action or the close Button press it
notes: The region is aria-live=polite: a new toast is read once, title then description, without moving focus.
Timers pause while the pointer is over the region or focus is inside it, so a toast never leaves while it is being read or reached.
A toast never holds the only way to do something: its action repeats something reachable elsewhere (Undo, Retry, View).
Leaving from the keyboard (Escape, the close Button pressed with a key) is instant.

motion: arrive: slides in from its edge (--y from ±100% to its place) and fades in, over duration.slow with easing.out-strong; nothing plays for toasts present on first paint
the others make room: they glide to their new offset on the same timing; after a dismissal they start as the exit ends (removeDelay = duration.base), with no empty slot in between
leave: shorter, over duration.base with easing.out-strong: it slides back towards its edge and fades
keyboard: leaving after Escape or a key press is instant (kbd-instant)
reduced motion: no travel: a toast fades in place (opacity only, duration.slow in, duration.base out); position and stacking still apply

overlap: the toasts behind the newest show only their edge, their content hidden (opacity 0) so no text shows past the front toast; it fades back in when the stack expands (hover, focus), with the same timing
